expert.visuals_analysis:
[PLOT: roc_curve] The x-axis represents 1-Specificity (False Positive Rate) and the y-axis represents Sensitivity (True Positive Rate). A curve hugging the top-left corner indicates high sensitivity with low false positive rates. [PLOT: pr_curve] This plot displays Precision on the y-axis against Recall on the x-axis, highlighting how precision degrades as recall increases.
[PLOT: confusion_matrix] The matrix visualizes True Positives (TP), False Negatives (FN), False Positives (FP), and True Negatives (TN). A strong diagonal indicates good performance. [PLOT: corr_heatmap] This heatmap shows correlation coefficients between features; values near 1 or -1 indicate high linear dependence.
[PLOT: feature_importance] Bars represent the magnitude of each feature's contribution to model predictions, with color indicating directionality (positive/negative impact).

glossary.Recall: The proportion of actual positive cases correctly identified by the model; critical for avoiding false negatives.
glossary.Precision: The proportion of predicted positive cases that are actually correct; inversely related to false positives.
glossary.ROC-AUC: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve, measuring overall discriminative ability independent of threshold.
